summary: Explains conditionals on playbook or inventory variables: use | bool for string truthy values like 'yes', and use defined/undefined tests to skip or fail when variables are missing. No {{ }} needed in conditionals.
questions: How do I use a yes/no string variable in a when condition?
How do I fail a play if a required variable isn't set?
How do I run a task only if a variable is defined?
Why is my 'yes' string not treated as true?

answer_card.title: Conditionals based on variables
answer_card.answer_md:
Cast non-boolean values with `| bool`:

```yaml
vars:
  epic: true
  monumental: "yes"
tasks:
- shell: echo "epic!"
  when: epic or monumental | bool
- shell: echo "not epic"
  when: not epic
```

Check definition:

```yaml
- shell: echo "I've got '{{ foo }}'"
  when: foo is defined
- ansible.builtin.fail: msg="This play requires 'bar'"
  when: bar is undefined
```

No `{{ }}` needed in `when`.
